newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Dresdner profits up, sees firm 96 growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dresdner profits up, sees firm 96 growth.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG on Thursday reported a 29.7 percent rise in nine-month profits, despite a surprising drop in trading income, and stuck to its forecast for a solid double-digit rise in full-year earnings.

Germany's second-largest commercial bank reported nine-month operating profits of 1.89 billion marks ($1.25 billion), broadly in line with analysts' forecasts but marking a slowdown from the 44 percent growth achieved at the half-year stage.

Analysts expressed surprise at a 14.8 decline in own-account trading profits to 456.2 million marks in the period, especially after Dresdner showed trading earnings of 382 million marks after the first six months.
"The trading result was disappointing," said Dieter Hein, analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.

"This in effect means that Dresdner barely earned 100 million marks on its own account in the last six months," Hein said, referring to Dresdner's indication that it had earned some 400 million marks on its own account in the first quarter.

However, Dresdner said its year-end trading income should show a double-digit rise, once pending earnings were realised, and a spokesman later said the bank was confident of earning 200 million marks from trading in the last quarter, bringing the figure back in the range of analysts' forecasts.

Dresdner also said its chief executive Juergen Sarrazin was expecting "clear double digit growth in (operating) earnings for the full year", stressing the bank's nine-month operating earnings already nearly matched its full earnings for 1995.
The bank's spokesman specified that the profit rise would be more than "just 10 or 15 percent".

Markets reacted moderately, with Dresdner shares initially rising, then slipping 50 pfennigs to close bourse dealings at 40.50 marks, slightly weaker than the market trend, but broadly in line with the rest of the banking sector.
Hein and other analysts said they were looking forward to the bank's analysts' meeting next Monday to get more details. Dresdner did not hold a news conference on Thursday.

Net commission income rose 42 percent to 2.8 billion marks, largely boosted by the integration of Dresdner's British investment banking operation Kleinwort Benson, which also contributed to a 7.6 percent rise in net interest income to 4.997 billion marks.

Administrative costs leapt to 6.09 billion marks from 5.15 billion marks but Dresdner said that, not counting the Kleinwort integration, the increase would have been 4.9 percent, which analysts said was a reasonable development.
Dresdner announced plans to launch a direct banking unit in the second half of 1997, a long awaited move which follows a path already taken by its major rivals.

It gave no precise details on the direct banking venture but said it would stand out from the existing options on offer. In general, it would increase its use of technology and planned to reduce its regular branch network in a bid to cut costs.

Dresdner also said it expected its commissions from the Deutsche Telekom issue, Germany's largest ever public offering which takes place in November, to be in the double-digit millions of marks in the fourth quarter.
Dresdner, one of the three global coordinators for the flotation, last week launched a worldwide roadshow aimed at wooing institutional investors for the issue.
It said its loan loss provisions rose 9.7 percent to 857.2 million marks in the first nine months, largely due to mid-sized domestic corporate risks.
However, this was offset by unusually high income of 605 million marks from securities held in the liquidity portfolio, which German banks can set against provisions. ($1=1.5125 Mark)
